\caption{What the test shows in hazard terms and what it could have missed, for all ground nearest a settlement with a water-side name (\MatchWetPct{} of the cells) and for the ground within 500\,m of such a settlement. Only the first row is pre-specified; the rest are exploratory (amendments 2, 3 and 5 to 8, or not planned, footnote a). Contributions are on the scale of the pooled $R$, that is, the change in the Brier score of all cells divided by the terrain increment. $^{a}$~The increments on this ground (amendment 2) re-expressed on the pooled scale (not planned). $^{b}$~Effect injected on a latent indicator of truly water-related names, drawn with the misreading rates measured against recorded etymologies. $^{c}$~Leaks the outcome by construction (the cell itself is left out): an upper bound, not a possible reading of names. $^{d}$~Known for \RecurCovPct{} of the cells; zero with an indicator elsewhere. $^{e}$~AOIs and cells that radar can assess; built-up land and seasonal water are excluded. $^{f}$~Base models fixed; no-effect reference: the mean increment of reassigned names with the regional composition rebuilt (amendment 8); in parentheses, Monte Carlo 95\,\% intervals over the simulated replicates (\PlasRepsA{} for all ground, \PlasRepsB{} within 500\,m). Bounds with other references are in Table~\STabEightBounds{} of the Supplement. $^{g}$~Within 500\,m, the interval is from a pairs cluster bootstrap over location groups (2,000 replicates). $^{h}$~Three injected odds ratios (\PlasRefOrMin{} to \PlasRefOrMax), three replicates each (amendment 7); translations and bounds with refitted models would therefore be slightly larger than those with the base models fixed. They are not read off this simulation because it has no effect below an odds ratio of \PlasRefOrMin{} (amendment 8, addendum 9).}\label{tab:hazard}
